review_comments.body:
### Bug: Command injection via unsanitized filename in shell command The `filename` parameter is wrapped in double quotes and concatenated directly into shell commands executed via `exec` and `execSync`. This allows command injection attacks because shell command substitution using `$(...)` or backticks still executes within double quotes, and attackers can escape the quotes. An attacker can execute arbitrary system commands by crafting a malicious filename.
Additional Locations (2) - [`lib/pdfinfo.js#L25-L26`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3746-unfixed-bugbot/blob/e8f906b5dad6d7a27c8953c1f6142c68a97b1054/lib/pdfinfo.js#L25-L26) - [`lib/pdfinfo.js#L35-L36`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3746-unfixed-bugbot/blob/e8f906b5dad6d7a27c8953c1f6142c68a97b1054/lib/pdfinfo.js#L35-L36)

### Bug: Incorrect typeof comparison always evaluates to true The condition `typeof optionArray.length !== undefined` is incorrect. The `typeof` operator returns a string (like `"number"` or `"undefined"`), so comparing it to the primitive value `undefined` with `!==` always evaluates to true. The comparison should use the string `"undefined"` or check `optionArray.length !== undefined` directly.

### Bug: Typo causes undefined passed to error callback The variable `self.options.addtional` is misspelled (missing an 'i'). It should be `self.options.additional`. This causes `undefined` to be passed as the third argument to the error callback instead of the actual options array.

### Bug: Wrong error property results in undefined message The code accesses `err.msg` but JavaScript Error objects have a `message` property, not `msg`. This causes the thrown error to include `undefined` in its message instead of the actual error details.

### Bug: Option values with spaces are truncated after split When `add_options` processes an option string containing spaces, it splits by space but only pushes the first two elements (`values[0]` and `values[1]`). Any additional parts are discarded. For example, an option like `-opw my password` would only capture `-opw` and `my`, silently losing `password`. This causes data truncation for values containing spaces.

### Bug: Unsanitized fileName allows path traversal to arbitrary files The `fileName` parameter is only checked with `fs.existsSync()` but lacks path traversal validation. When this function is called from `errorOverlayMiddleware.js` with user-controlled input from `req.query.fileName`, an attacker can specify any existing file path on the system (e.g., `/etc/passwd`, `../../../../sensitive/file`). The file would then be opened in the developer's editor, potentially exposing sensitive system or configuration files through CSRF attacks against the local development server.

### Bug: TypeError when REACT_EDITOR contains shell operators The `shellQuote.parse()` function returns objects (not strings) for shell operators like `&&`, `||`, `;`, and `|`. If `REACT_EDITOR` contains such operators (e.g., `&& code` or `; vim`), the first element returned could be an object like `{ op: '&&' }`. This object is truthy, so it passes the `if (!editor)` check, but then calling `editor.toLowerCase()` throws a `TypeError` because objects lack that method. The code assumes `editor` is always a string when it may not be.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/react-dev-utils/launchEditor.js#L179-L180`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-6342-unfixed-bugbot/blob/842fa7c24f87aac1e53897c6bb916149fa00c1d4/packages/react-dev-utils/launchEditor.js#L179-L180)

### Bug: Whitelist regex missing colon breaks Windows paths The `WINDOWS_FILE_NAME_WHITELIST` regex does not include the colon character (`:`), which is required for Windows drive letter paths like `C:\Users\file.js`. The regex range `\x2D-9` covers characters 0x2D to 0x39, but colon is 0x3A. This causes the whitelist check at line 322 to reject all absolute Windows paths containing drive letters, effectively breaking the editor launch functionality on Windows for any file specified with an absolute path.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/react-dev-utils/launchEditor.js#L319-L322`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-6342-fixed-bugbot/blob/1ba60cfeeeb3ea78c797848cb8dd443f3f14a5be/packages/react-dev-utils/launchEditor.js#L319-L322)

### Bug: Code injection via prototype pollution in `deleteFunctions` The `deleteFunctions` function uses a `for...in` loop to iterate over object properties without checking ownership via `hasOwnProperty`. This allows attackers to inject arbitrary code through prototype pollution - if `Object.prototype` is polluted with function properties, the iteration will include those inherited properties. When `options.ignoreFunction` is enabled and the serializer processes user-controlled objects, this can lead to arbitrary code injection. This is the known vulnerability CVE-2020-7660.
Additional Locations (1) - [`index.js#L66-L69`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2020-7660-unfixed-bugbot/blob/a22696ba83b009217bd98b375b2098fd10b87603/index.js#L66-L69)

### Bug: Global flag on regex causes inconsistent native code detection The `IS_NATIVE_CODE_REGEXP` regex has the global `g` flag, causing it to maintain `lastIndex` state between `.test()` calls. This makes the native code check in `serializeFunc` inconsistent - after a successful match, the next call to `.test()` on the same or different input may incorrectly return `false` because matching starts from the previous `lastIndex` position. This could allow native functions to bypass the security check on alternating calls.
Additional Locations (1) - [`index.js#L114-L115`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2020-7660-unfixed-bugbot/blob/a22696ba83b009217bd98b375b2098fd10b87603/index.js#L114-L115)

review_comments.body: ### Bug: TypeError when `deleteFunctions` receives null or undefined The `deleteFunctions(value)` call happens before the falsy value check on line 71. When `options.ignoreFunction` is true and `value` is `null` or `undefined`, the `for...in` loop inside `deleteFunctions` will throw a TypeError because it cannot convert null/undefined to an object. The falsy value guard needs to occur before the `deleteFunctions` call to prevent this crash.

### Bug: Unescaped RegExp flags enables arbitrary code injection This is CVE-2020-7660. When serializing RegExp objects, the `flags` property is directly interpolated into the output string without sanitization, while the `source` is properly serialized. If an attacker can control the RegExp object (e.g., via a Proxy with a malicious `flags` getter), they can inject arbitrary JavaScript code that will be executed when the serialized output is evaluated. The flags should be escaped or passed through `serialize()` like the source is.

### Bug: Global regex flag causes stateful test behavior The `IS_NATIVE_CODE_REGEXP` regex has the `g` (global) flag, making it stateful via `lastIndex`. When used with `.test()` in `serializeFunc`, consecutive calls serializing native functions may incorrectly pass the check after the first detection, because `lastIndex` advances past the match position. The `g` flag is unnecessary here since only detection (not iteration) is needed.
Additional Locations (1) - [`index.js#L126-L127`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2020-7660-fixed-bugbot/blob/7f4719fec97a81d6c3240c3c8e9572ab2dd2c191/index.js#L126-L127)

### Bug: Serialize mutates input objects unexpectedly when ignoring functions When `ignoreFunction` option is true, the `deleteFunctions` function is called on each `value` in the replacer callback. Since `value` is a reference to nested objects in the original input, this permanently mutates the caller's object by deleting function properties from nested objects. Serialization functions are typically expected to be pure and not modify their input, making this an unexpected side effect that could cause subtle bugs in calling code.
Additional Locations (1) - [`index.js#L45-L56`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2020-7660-fixed-bugbot/blob/7f4719fec97a81d6c3240c3c8e9572ab2dd2c191/index.js#L45-L56)

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Incorrect typeof comparison always evaluates to true The condition `typeof optionArray.length !== undefined` is always true. The `typeof` operator returns a string (like `"undefined"` or `"number"`), and comparing a string to the primitive value `undefined` using `!==` will never match. This means the check provides no protection. The fix requires either comparing to the string `'undefined'` with quotes, or using `optionArray.length !== undefined` without `typeof`.

### Bug: Error property uses `msg` instead of `message` The code references `err.msg` but JavaScript Error objects have a `message` property, not `msg`. This causes the error message to include `undefined` instead of the actual error description, making debugging difficult when `pdfinfo` fails.

### Bug: Typo `addtional` causes undefined callback parameter The property name `addtional` is misspelled and should be `additional`. Since `self.options.addtional` doesn't exist, the callback receives `undefined` as its third argument in error cases, while success cases correctly pass `self.options.additional`. This inconsistency could break error handling logic that relies on this parameter.

### Bug: Registered success and error callbacks are never invoked The `.success()` and `.error()` fluent methods store callbacks in `this.options.success` and `this.options.error`, but these callbacks are never actually invoked. The `getInfo` method only calls the `cb` parameter passed directly to it, ignoring the stored callbacks entirely. This makes the fluent callback API non-functional.

### Bug: Option split discards values after second space When an option string contains spaces, `split(' ')` creates an array of all parts, but only `values[0]` and `values[1]` are pushed to the arguments. Any additional parts are silently discarded. For example, an option like `-opw my password` would lose `password` entirely, causing incorrect command arguments.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: ReDoS vulnerability in header value regex splitting The regex `/ *, */` used in `split()` to parse header values is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (CVE-2017-16136). When an attacker sends a request with a header value containing a very long string of spaces without commas, the regex causes excessive CPU consumption due to backtracking. This can be exploited to hang the server and deny service to legitimate users.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: XML encoding only replaces first character occurrence (XSS) The `xmlEncode` function uses `String.replace()` with string arguments instead of regex with global flag, causing only the first occurrence of each special character to be encoded. For example, `""` becomes `"<script>alert(1)</script>"` where subsequent `<` and `>` characters remain unencoded. This enables cross-site scripting attacks when encoding user-controlled input. This is CVE-2019-10785.

### Bug: createElement lacks attribute value encoding allowing injection The `createElement` function directly concatenates attribute values into XML output without encoding them. Malicious attribute values containing quotes or special characters can break out of the attribute context and inject arbitrary attributes or content, enabling attribute injection attacks.

### Bug: decodeJid regex matches unhandled patterns causing data corruption The regex `/\\([23][02367acef])/g` in `decodeJid` matches more escape sequences than the switch statement handles. Patterns like `\2a`, `\2c`, `\2e`, `\30`, `\32`, `\33`, `\36`, `\37`, and `\3f` match the regex but have no corresponding switch case, causing them to be replaced with the literal string `"ARG"`. This corrupts data when JIDs contain backslash sequences that match the regex but aren't valid XEP-0106 escape codes.

### Bug: Prototype pollution via unvalidated object keys The `deepExtend` function is vulnerable to prototype pollution (CVE-2018-3750). When iterating through object keys at line 104, the code doesn't filter out dangerous keys like `__proto__` or `constructor`. If an attacker controls input (e.g., via `JSON.parse`), they can pass `{"__proto__": {"polluted": true}}` which causes the function to modify `Object.prototype` at line 137 via `target[key] = deepExtend(src, val)`, affecting all objects in the application.

### Bug: Prototype pollution via constructor.prototype path The `safeGetProperty` function only blocks access to `__proto__` but doesn't protect against the `constructor.prototype` prototype pollution attack vector. An attacker can pass an object like `{"constructor": {"prototype": {"polluted": true}}}` which will recursively traverse through `target.constructor` (which is `Object`) and then `Object.prototype`, ultimately polluting the prototype of all objects. This is the CVE-2018-3750 vulnerability.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/deep-extend.js#L103-L140`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3750-fixed-bugbot/blob/3f9bd7bdb679a5aa262ae9e948c73093ff911f15/lib/deep-extend.js#L103-L140)

### Bug: Missing null check for target causes TypeError The input validation at line 83 checks `typeof arguments[0] !== 'object'` but doesn't check for `null`. Since `typeof null === 'object'` in JavaScript, passing `null` as the first argument passes validation, then causes a TypeError when the code attempts to set properties on `null` at `target[key] = val`. This contradicts the documented behavior of returning `false` for incorrect types, and the source object check at line 100 correctly handles this case with `|| obj === null`.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Stream flush callback never called causing completion issues The `flush` function in the `mdToHtml` through2 stream receives a callback `cb` but never calls it. In through2 streams, both transform and flush callbacks must invoke their callbacks to properly signal completion. While `self.push(null)` ends the readable side, not calling `cb()` prevents proper stream finalization, which could cause the 'finish' event to not fire and lead to downstream consumers hanging or cleanup operations not completing properly.

### Bug: Prototype pollution vulnerability via `__proto__` manipulation The `setProperty` function has incomplete prototype pollution protection (CVE-2018-16491). When `Object.defineProperty` is unavailable, the fallback at line 28 (`target[name] = value`) allows direct `__proto__` assignment, enabling attackers to pollute `Object.prototype` via payloads like `{"__proto__": {"polluted": true}}` during deep extend operations. This can lead to property injection across all objects in the application.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/extend.js#L93-L98`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-16491-fixed-bugbot/blob/39d8233ea5d3e7fa844708135a21bd3af989efe7/lib/extend.js#L93-L98)

### Bug: Incomplete `getProperty` fallthrough for `__proto__` handling The `getProperty` function has incomplete control flow when handling `__proto__`. When `name === '__proto__'`, `has(obj, name)` is true, but `gOPD` is unavailable, the function falls through to `return obj[name]` at line 44 instead of having an explicit return. This causes `obj['__proto__']` to return the prototype object rather than the own property value, defeating the intended special handling and contributing to incorrect behavior in environments without `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`.

### Bug: Environment variable leakage through debug print functions The `print_options` and `plugin_options` functions expose sensitive data by printing the entire options object to console using `Util.inspect` with `{ depth: null }`. Environment variables parsed into the options (like `SENECA_OPTIONS`) can contain secrets such as API keys or passwords. When `--seneca.print.options` is passed on the command line, this sensitive data gets logged. This is CVE-2019-5483 - environment variable leakage in Seneca.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/print.js#L140-L151`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2019-5483-fixed-bugbot/blob/7bc31863bf433b9db50fa680c12bacaa770f93a2/lib/print.js#L140-L151)

### Bug: Duplicate 'seneca' value in role filter condition The value `'seneca'` is checked twice in the role filter condition - once on line 82 and again on line 90. The second occurrence is redundant and likely a copy-paste error. This suggests another role value was intended for line 90 but was accidentally duplicated, potentially leaving a role unfiltered that should have been excluded from the tree output.

### Bug: Unsafe property access on meta.func may crash The code accesses `meta.func.name` without checking if `meta.func` is defined. While the `while (meta)` loop ensures `meta` is truthy, if the action metadata has a null or undefined `func` property, this would throw a TypeError and crash the print operation. The `meta.plugin_fullname` access on line 106 uses a fallback with `|| '-'`, but `meta.func` does not have similar defensive handling.

### Bug: Ajv `allErrors` enables denial of service via resource exhaustion The `allErrors: true` option in the Ajv configuration (CVE-2020-8192) allows attackers to trigger resource exhaustion. When this option is enabled, Ajv collects all validation errors instead of failing fast on the first error. A malicious user can craft inputs that generate exponentially many validation errors, causing memory and CPU exhaustion leading to denial of service.

### Bug: Falsy coerced values are not applied to request The condition `ret && ret.value` fails to apply coerced values when they are falsy (like `0`, `''`, `false`, or `null`). When a Joi-style validator successfully coerces input to a falsy value, the check evaluates to false and the coerced value is never assigned to `request[paramName]`. The check needs to verify the presence of the `value` property rather than its truthiness.

### Bug: Custom options can override allErrors security setting The `Object.assign` call places `options.customOptions` after the default options, allowing user-provided custom options to override the security-critical `allErrors: false` setting. Despite the comment warning that setting `allErrors: true` enables a DoS attack, a malicious user can pass `{ allErrors: true }` in `customOptions` to override the safe default. This is CVE-2020-8192 - a denial of service vulnerability that allows resource exhaustion through specially crafted schemas when `allErrors` is enabled.

### Bug: Negative length causes infinite loop in generation The `while (length--)` loop will run infinitely if `length` is negative. In JavaScript, negative numbers are truthy, and decrementing them makes them more negative rather than approaching zero. If a caller passes a negative length like `randomatic('a', -5)`, the application will hang indefinitely. The loop condition doesn't guard against non-positive values.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: SQL injection via improper identifier escaping in MSSQL The `wrapIdentifierImpl` function improperly sanitizes SQL identifiers by stripping bracket and quote characters (`[`, `]`, `'`) instead of properly escaping them. In MSSQL, closing brackets in bracketed identifiers must be escaped by doubling them (`]` → `]]`). The current approach of character removal allows attackers to craft malicious input that breaks out of the identifier context, enabling SQL injection. This is the exact pattern described in CVE-2019-10757.

If a RegExp contains a `"` character in its source, it can break out of the string delimiter and inject arbitrary JavaScript code. review_comments.body: ### Bug: Path traversal vulnerability allows reading arbitrary files The `filePath` is constructed by directly concatenating `process.cwd()` with the URL pathname without any sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences like `../` in the URL to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files from the filesystem (e.g., `GET /../../../etc/passwd`). This is the exact vulnerability described in CVE-2017-16029. The path needs to be normalized and validated to ensure it stays within the intended directory.

### Bug: Last-Modified header incorrectly set to future date The `Last-Modified` header is set to a future date (`Date.now() + _expirationTime * 1000`) instead of the file's actual modification time (`stat.mtime`). Per HTTP specifications, `Last-Modified` must indicate when the resource was last modified, not an expiration time. This breaks HTTP caching semantics and would cause clients to incorrectly cache resources.

### Bug: Cache validation compares wrong values for If-Modified-Since The `matchExpiration` calculation compares `If-Modified-Since` against `Date.now()` instead of the file's actual modification time (`stat.mtime`). HTTP conditional requests require comparing the client's cached timestamp against when the file was actually modified. The current logic only returns 304 if the client's timestamp is in the future, which is semantically incorrect.

### Bug: Deprecated Buffer constructor may cause security issues Using the deprecated `new Buffer()` constructor instead of `Buffer.from()`. In older Node.js versions, the `Buffer` constructor with non-numeric arguments can expose uninitialized memory if passed certain inputs. While the array join here produces a string, using the deprecated API is a security anti-pattern and the constructor was deprecated specifically due to security concerns.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Path traversal sanitization is incomplete and bypassable The path traversal sanitization using `replace(/\/\.\./, "").replace(/\.\.\//, "")` is insufficient. The regex patterns lack the global flag (`g`), so only the first occurrence of `/..` or `../` is removed. An attacker can access files outside the intended directory by using paths like `/../../../etc/passwd` which becomes `/../../etc/passwd` after sanitization. This allows reading arbitrary files from the filesystem.

### Bug: Last-Modified header incorrectly set to future date The `Last-Modified` header is set to a future date (`Date.now() + _expirationTime * 1000`) instead of the resource's actual modification time (e.g., `stat.mtime`). Per HTTP RFC 7232, `Last-Modified` must indicate when the resource was last modified, not an expiration time. This breaks standard HTTP caching semantics and causes incorrect behavior with HTTP-compliant clients. The `matchExpiration` check also validates against current time rather than comparing modification dates.

review_comments.body:
### Bug: Command injection via unsanitized input in shell commands The `_buildCommand` method constructs shell commands by directly interpolating user-controlled values (`this.path`, `args`) into a template string without sanitization. These commands are executed via `child_process.exec()`, which runs them in a shell. An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands through parameters like `path` or `ref` (e.g., `; malicious-command` or `` `malicious-command` ``). This is the known vulnerability CVE-2017-1000451.
Additional Locations (2) - [`lib/index.ts#L37-L38`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2017-16087-unfixed-bugbot/blob/a2172a546b0e051e816232ce2e09681ac7d45d07/lib/index.ts#L37-L38) - [`lib/index.ts#L61-L64`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2017-16087-unfixed-bugbot/blob/a2172a546b0e051e816232ce2e09681ac7d45d07/lib/index.ts#L61-L64)

### Bug: Debug logging leaks command containing user input A `console.log(command)` statement is left in the error handling path of `revParse`. This debug statement logs the full git command which could contain sensitive user-supplied paths or refs to the console. Debug logging statements are typically removed before production deployment.

### Bug: Regex match result used without null check The `_lsTree` method calls `str.match()` and immediately accesses `matches[1]` through `matches[4]` without checking if the regex matched. If the git output contains a line that doesn't match the expected format, `matches` will be `null` and accessing its properties will throw a `TypeError`, crashing the application.

### Bug: Possible undefined return when git output is empty In `revParse`, the method returns `list[0]` after filtering empty lines, but if the filtered list is empty (e.g., git returns only whitespace or an empty response), `list[0]` will be `undefined`. The return type is `Promise` but an `undefined` value could be resolved, causing unexpected behavior in calling code like `_lsTree`.

### Bug: Missing forward slash in unsafe character regex causes XSS The `unsafeChars` regex doesn't include `/` (forward slash), even though `/` exists in the `escaped` map with proper escaping (`\u002F`). The `escapeUnsafeChars` function used by `safeKey` and `safeProp` only replaces characters matched by `unsafeChars`, so forward slashes in object keys won't be escaped. This is the root cause of CVE-2019-13506 - when serialized output is embedded in HTML script tags, unescaped forward slashes in object keys can contribute to XSS attacks.
Additional Locations (1) - [`src/index.ts#L227-L230`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2019-13506-unfixed-bugbot/blob/c063147beabeaa0ec9b9d343e926324ae85ae1b7/src/index.ts#L227-L230)

### Bug: Unquoted __proto__ keys enable prototype pollution attacks The identifier regex `/^[_$a-zA-Z][_$a-zA-Z0-9]*$/` in `safeKey` and `safeProp` matches `__proto__`, causing it to be output unquoted. When the serialized output is evaluated, object literals with unquoted `__proto__` keys actually modify the object's prototype in JavaScript. This enables prototype pollution attacks, as objects like `{__proto__: {isAdmin: true}}` serialize to code that sets the prototype rather than creating a normal property.

The code joins method calls with `.` but for empty collections, `Array.from(thing)` returns an empty array, causing `.join('.')` to return an empty string. This produces output like `a.` followed by a semicolon, which is a syntax error (e.g., `(function(a){a.;return [a,a]}(new Set))`).

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Null reference when regex match fails in _lsTree The `_lsTree` method calls `str.match()` and immediately accesses `matches[1]`, `matches[2]`, etc. without checking if `matches` is null. If the regex doesn't match (due to malformed git output or unexpected data), `matches` will be `null` and accessing indexed properties will throw a `TypeError`. This causes the entire Promise chain to fail unexpectedly.

### Bug: User input passed unsanitized to shell commands User-controlled values (`path`, `ref`) are passed directly to git commands without sanitization via `_buildCommand`. While `execFile` is used instead of `exec`, malicious input could still be crafted to abuse git's argument parsing, potentially allowing access to unintended files or refs. This is the vulnerability pattern described in CVE-2017-1000451 for the fs-git package.
Additional Locations (2) - [`lib/index.ts#L55-L56`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2017-16087-fixed-bugbot/blob/7864c58e104b4e7776f29dc2d8734767dae5a8d4/lib/index.ts#L55-L56) - [`lib/index.ts#L93-L94`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2017-16087-fixed-bugbot/blob/7864c58e104b4e7776f29dc2d8734767dae5a8d4/lib/index.ts#L93-L94)

### Bug: Debug console.log left in error handling code A `console.log(command)` statement is present in the `revParse` error handler. This appears to be debug code that could leak sensitive information (git directory paths, refs) to logs in production environments.

### Bug: Undefined access when showRef output lacks space separator In `showRef`, the code splits each line by space with `str.split(" ", 2)` and accesses `columns[1]` without validation. If a line doesn't contain a space, `columns[1]` will be `undefined`, violating the `RefInfo` interface contract that specifies `name: string`. This produces incorrect data silently rather than handling the unexpected format appropriately.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: ReDoS vulnerability via unescaped regex from user input The `opts.replacement` value is user-controlled and used in a `String.prototype.replace()` call. This has two consequences: unescaped regex metacharacters can lead to catastrophic backtracking and a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attack (CVE-2017-16117), and the `$` character in the search pattern `opts.replacement + "$"` is interpreted literally, which prevents the intended removal of trailing separators.

### Bug: Path traversal protection completely broken by indexOf misuse The `cleanUrl` function's path traversal protection is completely non-functional. `String.indexOf()` returns a number (the index position), not a string, so calling `.length` on it returns `undefined`. Since `undefined > 0` is always `false`, the while loop never executes. Attackers can use `..` sequences to traverse directories and access arbitrary files outside the intended path.

### Bug: Trailing slash removal logic doesn't actually remove slash The code attempts to remove trailing slashes from the URL but `url.slice(0, url.length)` returns the entire string unchanged. The second argument should be `url.length - 1` to actually strip the trailing character. This prevents proper URL normalization.

### Bug: XSS vulnerability from unsanitized file names in HTML File names are embedded directly into HTML output without any escaping or sanitization. If a file has a malicious name containing HTML or JavaScript (e.g., `<script>alert(1)</script>.txt`), the code will execute in users' browsers when they view the directory listing. This is a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability.

### Bug: Cache-Control header overwritten, losing important directives The second `setHeader("Cache-Control", ...)` call overwrites the first one instead of combining them. This loses the important cache directives `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0` and only keeps `post-check=0, pre-check=0`. The values need to be combined into a single header value to apply all cache control directives.
Additional Locations (1) - [`crud-file-server.js#L101-L103`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3726-unfixed-bugbot/blob/af302f45663a82a78818decc0d2f77e27112286d/crud-file-server.js#L101-L103)

### Bug: HEAD requests incorrectly blocked in readOnly mode The condition `req.method != 'GET'` blocks HEAD requests when `readOnly` is true, but HEAD is a safe, read-only HTTP method that retrieves only headers without a response body. The condition needs to allow both GET and HEAD methods in read-only mode.

### Bug: Path traversal protection completely broken by type error The `cleanUrl` function's path traversal protection is entirely ineffective. The condition `url.indexOf('..').length > 0` is checking `.length` on a number (since `indexOf` returns a number, not a string). This evaluates to `undefined`, and `undefined > 0` is always `false`, so the while loop never executes. This allows attackers to use `..` sequences to traverse directories and access files outside the intended path.

### Bug: Trailing slash removal does not actually remove slash The code intended to remove a trailing slash from the URL uses `url.slice(0, url.length)`, which returns the entire string unchanged. To actually remove the trailing character, it needs to use `url.slice(0, url.length - 1)`. This causes URLs with trailing slashes to not be properly normalized.

### Bug: Cache-Control header overwritten, losing critical no-cache directives Calling `res.setHeader("Cache-Control", ...)` twice with different values causes the second call to overwrite the first. The important directives `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0` are lost, and only `post-check=0, pre-check=0` (IE-specific extensions) remains. These values need to be combined into a single header value.
Additional Locations (1) - [`crud-file-server.js#L101-L103`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3726-fixed-bugbot/blob/45c6156bcf7869d765a3c382575a8594c14289ee/crud-file-server.js#L101-L103)

### Bug: Authorization header leaks to redirect domains via requestOptions The redirect handling deletes the authorization header from the local `headers` variable when redirecting to a different hostname, but `_mergeHeaders` is called again in `_prepareRequest` during redirects. Since `_mergeHeaders` merges `this.requestOptions.headers` with the passed `headers`, any authorization header originally set in `requestOptions.headers` will be re-included in the merged result. This causes authorization headers to leak to redirect target domains, which is the CVE-2020-11021 vulnerability.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Missing return after resolve causes duplicate promise settlement When `statusCode` equals `HttpCodes.NotFound` (404), `resolve(response)` is called but execution continues without returning. The code then reads the body and, since 404 > 299, enters the error handling block and calls `reject(err)`. While the first settlement wins in JavaScript promises, this causes unnecessary body processing and attempts to reject an already-resolved promise. A `return` statement is missing after `resolve(response)`.

+      // we don't want to set NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 since that will affect request for entire process
+      // http.RequestOptions doesn't expose a way to modify RequestOptions.agent.options
+      // we have to cast it to any and change it directly
+      agent.options = Object.assign(agent.options || {}, {
+        rejectUnauthorized: false
+      })
+    }
+
+    return agent
+  }
+
+  private _performExponentialBackoff(retryNumber: number): Promise<void> {
+    retryNumber = Math.min(ExponentialBackoffCeiling, retryNumber)
+    const ms: number = ExponentialBackoffTimeSlice * Math.pow(2, retryNumber)
+    return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(() => resolve(), ms))
+  }
+
+  private static dateTimeDeserializer(key: any, value: any): any {
+    if (typeof value === 'string') {
+      let a = new Date(value)
+      if (!isNaN(a.valueOf())) {
+        return a
+      }
+    }
+
+    return value
+  }
+
+  private async _processResponse<T>(
+    res: ifm.IHttpClientResponse,
+    options: ifm.IRequestOptions
+  ): Promise<ifm.ITypedResponse<T>> {
+    return new Promise<ifm.ITypedResponse<T>>(async (resolve, reject) => {
+      const statusCode: number = res.message.statusCode
+
+      const response: ifm.ITypedResponse<T> = {
+        statusCode: statusCode,
+        result: null,
+        headers: {}
+      }
+
+      // not found leads to null obj returned
+      if (statusCode == HttpCodes.NotFound) {
+        resolve(response)
+      }

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Arbitrary code injection via unsanitized eval The `performAction` function in case 39 uses `eval("[" + yytext + "]")` where `yytext` contains user-controlled input from the parser. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript code by crafting malicious formula input that escapes the array context (e.g., `1]; maliciousCode(); [1`). This is CVE-2020-6836, a known code injection vulnerability in formula parsers that allows remote code execution.

### Bug: Parser vulnerable to arbitrary code injection (CVE-2020-6836) This file is a Jison-generated parser from a vulnerable version of `hot-formula-parser` that contains CVE-2020-6836, a critical arbitrary code injection vulnerability (CVSS 9.8). The `performAction` function passes unsanitized user input to functions like `yy.callVariable()`, `yy.callFunction()`, and `yy.evaluateByOperator()` without proper sanitization. Attackers can inject and execute arbitrary code through crafted formula input, potentially leading to remote code execution.

### Bug: Wrong property reference breaks lexer backtracking state backup When saving lexer context for backtracking, `this.last_line` is used instead of `this.yylloc.last_line`. The property `this.last_line` does not exist on the lexer object - all other `yylloc` properties in this same backup object correctly reference `this.yylloc.first_line`, `this.yylloc.first_column`, and `this.yylloc.last_column`. This causes the backed-up `yylloc.last_line` to be `undefined`, resulting in incorrect state restoration when the lexer backtracks with `backtrack_lexer` enabled.

### Bug: Wrong object used for error message property The code uses `res.message` to display error information, but `res` is an HTTP `ServerResponse` object which doesn't have a `message` property. The error message is available on the `err` object as `err.message`. This results in `undefined` being displayed in the HTML heading when errors occur.
Additional Locations (1) - [`bin/public#L99-L100`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3747-unfixed-bugbot/blob/4a1b43350df9ff99e6b088099984f8102d77b804/bin/public#L99-L100)

### Bug: Condition checks wrong variable causing dead code The condition `if (path)` checks whether the `path` module (required at line 5) is truthy, which is always true. This makes the condition meaningless and the `else` branch at line 122-123 unreachable dead code. The intended check was likely `if (dir)` or `if (root)` to validate the directory path.

### Bug: Path traversal check bypassable via directory prefix The path traversal protection using `abs.indexOf(root) !== 0` can be bypassed. If `root` is `/var/www`, a path resolving to `/var/www-evil/file` would pass the check because the string starts with `/var/www`. A secure check would verify the path starts with `root + path.sep` or equals `root` exactly.

### Bug: String replace removes wrong dot character in paths The `filePath.replace(dir, '')` operation is flawed when `dir` is `.` (the default). The `replace` method with a string argument matches the first occurrence anywhere in the string, so for a path like `somedir/file.txt`, it removes the `.` from the file extension instead of the directory prefix, producing `somedir/filetxt`. This breaks the generated links in directory listings.

### Bug: XSS vulnerability via unescaped file names in HTML File names and directory paths are directly concatenated into HTML output without any escaping. A maliciously named file containing HTML/JavaScript (e.g., ``) would execute arbitrary code in users' browsers when they view the directory listing, enabling cross-site scripting attacks.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Trailing separator removal uses literal string instead of regex The code `result.replace(opts.replacement+"$",'')` is intended to remove a trailing separator (as the comment states), but it doesn't work correctly. In JavaScript, `String.prototype.replace()` with a string first argument performs a literal string match, not a regex match. So when `opts.replacement` is `"-"`, the code looks for the literal string `"-$"` instead of matching `"-"` at the end of the string. This means trailing separators like `"hello-"` won't be cleaned up as intended.

### Bug: Empty string charmap values ignored due to falsy check The check `if (opts.charmap[char])` uses truthiness to determine if a character has a mapping. However, the charmap contains entries with empty string values (e.g., `'ь':''` at line 111 and `'Ь':''` at line 116). Since empty strings are falsy in JavaScript, these legitimate mappings are ignored, and the code falls through to the `else` branch treating them as unmapped characters. The check needs to use `char in opts.charmap` or `opts.charmap[char] !== undefined` instead.

### Bug: Invalid mode causes TypeError when accessing defaults When `opts.mode` is set to a value that doesn't exist in `slug.defaults.modes`, the variable `defaults` becomes `undefined`. Subsequent accesses to `defaults[key]` on line 21 and `defaults.symbols` on line 24 will throw a TypeError. There's no validation that the mode is valid before using it to look up the defaults object.

### Bug: Multicharmap empty string values would be ignored Similar to the charmap issue, the check `if (opts.multicharmap[str])` uses truthiness. If a multicharmap entry maps to an empty string, this check would fail and treat the multi-character sequence as unmatched. While the default multicharmap doesn't have empty values, user-provided options could, leading to unexpected behavior.

### Bug: Prototype pollution via unsanitized path traversal The `set` function allows arbitrary property assignment without validating path parts against dangerous properties like `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`. An attacker can pass a path such as `__proto__.polluted` to pollute `Object.prototype`, affecting all objects in the application. This is CVE-2018-16490 - the code lacks sanitization to prevent prototype pollution during property traversal and assignment via `obj[part] = map(val)`.
Additional Locations (2) - [`lib/index.js#L248-L249`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-16490-unfixed-bugbot/blob/438d42bc10c824e7f68b4d0ad111803eb724b15c/lib/index.js#L248-L249) - [`lib/index.js#L260-L261`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-16490-unfixed-bugbot/blob/438d42bc10c824e7f68b4d0ad111803eb724b15c/lib/index.js#L260-L261)

### Bug: Falsy values cause premature path traversal termination The check `if (!obj)` terminates path traversal for any falsy value including legitimate values like `0`, `false`, and `''`. For example, `get('a.b', {a: 0})` returns `0` instead of `undefined`, and `set('a.b', 'x', {a: 0})` silently fails to set anything. The check conflates "value is falsy" with "cannot continue traversal" - it needs to distinguish `null`/`undefined` from other falsy values.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/index.js#L226-L227`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-16490-unfixed-bugbot/blob/438d42bc10c824e7f68b4d0ad111803eb724b15c/lib/index.js#L226-L227)

### Bug: Empty array path creates property named "undefined" When `path` is an empty array `[]`, `len` becomes `-1` and `parts[len]` evaluates to `parts[-1]` which is `undefined`. This causes `obj[undefined]` assignment at line 272, creating a property literally named `"undefined"` on the object. The code lacks validation for empty paths before attempting to access the last element.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Unauthenticated endpoint allows remote service shutdown The `/_ah/stop` endpoint exposes Chrome instance termination to any remote attacker without authentication. Any unauthorized user can send a GET request to this endpoint and kill the Chrome process, causing a denial of service for all users. This is the CVE-2017-18353 vulnerability.

### Bug: Promise catch swallows error causing undefined result The inline `.catch()` on `renderer.captureScreenshot()` logs the error but returns `undefined`, which is then assigned to `result`. The code continues to execute `new Buffer(result, 'base64')` with `undefined`, causing unexpected behavior. The outer try-catch won't catch this because the promise rejection was already handled. This pattern differs from the `/render/` route which correctly uses only try-catch.

### Bug: SSRF allows access to internal resources and files The `/render/` and `/screenshot/` endpoints accept arbitrary user-supplied URLs without proper validation. The `isRestricted` function only works when `config['renderOnly']` is explicitly configured, which is optional. Without this, attackers can access internal services (localhost, internal IPs), cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or local files via `file://` protocol.
Additional Locations (1) - [`src/main.js#L109-L132`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2017-18353-unfixed-bugbot/blob/b1cb0c06d6ec5ff72527245aab5277f3f5e5009a/src/main.js#L109-L132)

### Bug: Reflected XSS via unsanitized URL in error response The error messages include `request.params.url` directly in the response without sanitization. Express's `.send()` method defaults to `Content-Type: text/html` for strings, allowing attackers to inject malicious JavaScript via the URL parameter. This is CVE-2017-18352 - reflected Cross-Site Scripting from invalid URLs.
Additional Locations (1) - [`src/main.js#L126-L130`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2017-18353-unfixed-bugbot/blob/b1cb0c06d6ec5ff72527245aab5277f3f5e5009a/src/main.js#L126-L130)

### Bug: Chrome debugging port exposed to all network interfaces The `--remote-debugging-address=0.0.0.0` flag binds Chrome's DevTools Protocol to all network interfaces. This allows any external attacker on the network to connect to the Chrome debugging port and execute arbitrary commands, access page contents, or take control of the browser session.

### Bug: Deprecated Buffer constructor has security implications The `new Buffer()` constructor is deprecated since Node.js 6.x due to security concerns - it can expose sensitive memory contents when passed a number instead of a string. When `result` is `undefined` (from the swallowed error), `new Buffer(undefined, 'base64')` behavior is unpredictable. Using `Buffer.from()` is the safe alternative.

### Bug: Missing null check before killing Chrome instance The `/_ah/stop` endpoint calls `config.chrome.kill()` without checking if `config.chrome` exists. If this endpoint is called before Chrome has finished launching (before line 146 executes), `config.chrome` will be undefined, causing an unhandled error and potential server crash.

### Bug: Incomplete prototype pollution protection allows constructor bypass The prototype pollution protection in `exports.set` only blocks `__proto__` but not `constructor`. An attacker can bypass this by using a path like `constructor.prototype.polluted` to modify `Object.prototype`, polluting all objects in the application. The same incomplete protection exists in `exports.unset`. This is exactly CVE-2018-16490 - the `constructor` property needs to be blocked alongside `__proto__` to prevent prototype pollution attacks.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/index.js#L136-L140`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-16490-fixed-bugbot/blob/19f843f63ff7784b1b1c766afb7b8d4e696284f7/lib/index.js#L136-L140)

### Bug: Falsy value checks cause incorrect path traversal termination The condition `!obj` incorrectly treats legitimate falsy values (`0`, `false`, `''`) as missing values, causing premature return. For example, `get('a.b.c', { a: { b: 0 } })` returns `0` instead of `undefined` because the loop exits early when `obj` becomes `0`. The check should use `obj == null` to only exit for `null`/`undefined`. The same issue occurs at line 66-68 where falsy array items return `map(undefined)` instead of continuing traversal, and at line 239 in the `set` function.
Additional Locations (2) - [`lib/index.js#L65-L68`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-16490-fixed-bugbot/blob/19f843f63ff7784b1b1c766afb7b8d4e696284f7/lib/index.js#L65-L68) - [`lib/index.js#L238-L239`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-16490-fixed-bugbot/blob/19f843f63ff7784b1b1c766afb7b8d4e696284f7/lib/index.js#L238-L239)

### Bug: Falsy array items silently skipped during set operations The conditions `if (item)` at lines 256 and 268 skip setting properties on array items that are falsy values like `0`, `false`, or `''`. This causes silent data loss when trying to set properties on arrays containing these values. For instance, setting a path on `[0, { x: 1 }]` would only modify the second element, leaving the first unchanged. The checks should use `if (item != null)` to only skip `null`/`undefined` items.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/index.js#L267-L268`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-16490-fixed-bugbot/blob/19f843f63ff7784b1b1c766afb7b8d4e696284f7/lib/index.js#L267-L268)

The call to `exports.enable(load())` passes the user-controlled `process.env.DEBUG` environment variable to the `enable()` function, which constructs RegExp objects from user input without proper escaping of special regex characters. An attacker can set a malicious DEBUG value to cause Regular Expression Denial of Service.

### Bug: Path traversal vulnerability allows directory access bypass The path traversal protection has a critical ordering flaw. The `decodeURIComponent` call on line 193 occurs **after** the traversal check on line 183, meaning double-encoded path sequences could bypass validation. Additionally, the traversal regex `[\/\\]\.\.[\/\\]` requires slashes on both sides of `..`, missing edge cases where `..` appears at path boundaries without a trailing slash. This is the known CVE-2017-16224 vulnerability that allows attackers to access files outside the intended directory via crafted URLs containing encoded traversal sequences.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Empty directories cause callback to never be invoked The `_loadReaddir` function has a logic flaw when handling empty directories. When `files.length` is 0 (empty directory or all files filtered out), `len` is set to 0 and `files.forEach` executes zero iterations, meaning `next()` is never called. review_comments.body: ### Bug: ReDoS vulnerability in formatter regex pattern The `exports.formatters.o` function in `src/node.js` contains a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability (CVE-2017-16137). The regex `/\s*\n\s*/g` can cause catastrophic backtracking when applied to `util.inspect()` output with many consecutive whitespace characters but no newlines. This can be triggered by untrusted input, leading to high CPU consumption and application unresponsiveness.

### Bug: Empty directory causes callback to never be invoked In `_loadReaddir`, when a directory is empty or all files are filtered out (e.g., hidden files with `dot: false`), the `files` array becomes empty. When `files.length` is 0, `forEach` never executes, so `next()` is never called, and `cb(null, data)` is never invoked. This causes the request to hang indefinitely when accessing an empty directory, as the async callback is never completed.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Path traversal vulnerability allows reading arbitrary files The `getUriPath` function has a path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2017-16224). The `decodeURIComponent` call on line 192 occurs AFTER the directory traversal check on line 182. This ordering allows specially crafted percent-encoded URL sequences to bypass the traversal detection, potentially enabling attackers to read arbitrary files from the server's filesystem. The path sanitization logic can be circumvented by using encoding patterns that aren't decoded until after the security check.

### Bug: Directory listing links broken for special character filenames The `name` variable is first HTML-escaped (replacing `"` with `"`, etc.) on lines 505-509, then `encodeURIComponent(name)` is called on line 513 to create `linkName`. This causes double-encoding where, for example, a file named `foo"bar` has `"` replaced with `"`, then URL-encoded to `foo%26quot%3Bbar` instead of the correct `foo%22bar`. The resulting links in directory listings will point to non-existent files for any filename containing `"`, `<`, `>`, or `'`.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: No-op regex fails to ensure leading slash The comment says "Make sure it starts with a slash" but the regex `p.replace(/^\//, '/')` is a no-op—it just replaces a leading `/` with `/`. If the path somehow lacks a leading slash (which could happen with malformed URLs or certain edge cases in `url.parse`), this code won't add one as intended. The regex pattern appears to be incorrect for the stated purpose.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Command injection via unsanitized shell execution The `run` function passes the `command` parameter directly to `execPromise` (promisified `exec`), which spawns a shell to execute commands. This enables command injection when user-controlled input is interpolated into command strings. The codebase uses this function with user-controlled values like `remoteUrl` and `tag` (e.g., `git clone ${remoteUrl}`), allowing attackers to inject arbitrary shell commands through these inputs. This is the CVE-2019-10776 vulnerability pattern.

### Bug: Missing error event handler causes unhandled promise rejection The `runWithSpawn` function doesn't handle the `error` event on the spawned child process. If `spawn` fails to start the process (e.g., command not found causing ENOENT, or permission denied), an `error` event is emitted but never caught. This can cause the promise to never resolve or reject, leading to hangs, or result in an unhandled error being thrown. The function only listens for `close` events, which may not fire when spawn itself fails.

### Bug: SSRF vulnerability allows access to internal resources The `isRestricted` function only validates that the URL protocol is `http` or `https`, but doesn't prevent access to internal network resources. Attackers can request URLs like `http://localhost/`, `http://127.0.0.1/`, `http://169.254.169.254/` (cloud metadata endpoints), or internal hostnames to perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks. The renderer will fetch these internal resources and return their content to the attacker.

### Bug: Catch handler swallows error causing undefined result The `.catch((err) => console.error(err))` on `renderer.captureScreenshot` swallows the rejection and returns `undefined`. When the screenshot fails, `result` becomes `undefined`, then `new Buffer(result, 'base64')` is called with `undefined`, causing a different error to be thrown. This differs from the `/render` endpoint which properly propagates errors, and results in misleading error messages and double-logging.

### Bug: Chrome remote debugging exposed to all network interfaces The `--remote-debugging-address=0.0.0.0` flag exposes Chrome's remote debugging interface to all network interfaces. If the server is accessible from a network, attackers could potentially connect to the Chrome debugging port and gain full control over the browser instance, enabling them to execute arbitrary JavaScript, access browsed content, or pivot to further attacks.

### Bug: Deprecated Buffer constructor poses security risk The `new Buffer()` constructor is deprecated since Node.js 6 due to security concerns. When the first argument is unexpectedly a number (which could happen if the screenshot result is malformed), `new Buffer(number)` creates an uninitialized buffer that may leak sensitive memory contents. The safe alternative is `Buffer.from(result, 'base64')` which consistently treats the input as a string.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Command injection via unsanitized input to shell exec The `run` function passes the `command` parameter directly to `execPromise` (which wraps `exec`), executing it in a shell. Throughout the codebase, callers construct commands using string interpolation with user-controlled variables like `tag`, `ignoredFile`, `startTag`, and `endTag`. This enables OS command injection attacks where malicious input containing shell metacharacters (e.g., `; rm -rf /` or backticks) can execute arbitrary commands. This is the pattern described in CVE-2019-10776.

### Bug: Inadequate URL sanitization allows XSS bypass The `trimRegExp` pattern `/[\s\^@-\^_]+/g` used to sanitize URLs before checking for `javascript:` schemes is incomplete. It only removes standard whitespace and ASCII control characters (0x00-0x1F), but doesn't strip other Unicode characters like `\u00A0` (non-breaking space), `\u2028` (line separator), or `\u2029` (paragraph separator). An attacker could craft URLs like `java\u00A0script:alert(1)` that bypass the `scriptUriRegExp` check because the non-standard whitespace character remains, yet browsers may still interpret this as a JavaScript URL, enabling cross-site scripting attacks. This is the known vulnerability CVE-2019-1010091.

### Bug: Bogus attribute check ignores single-quoted and unquoted values The `checkBogusAttribute` function only extracts the value from `matches[2]` (double-quoted values), but the `attrRegExp` captures single-quoted values in group 3 and unquoted values in group 4. This means for `data-mce-bogus='all'` or `data-mce-bogus=all`, the function returns `undefined` instead of `'all'`. The early optimization check at line 331-340 then fails to skip these elements properly because `undefined === 'all'` is false. While a backup check later compensates for this, the inconsistent behavior between `checkBogusAttribute` and `parseAttribute` (which correctly uses `value || val2 || val3`) represents a logic error.

### Bug: XSS vulnerability via unsanitized HTML in dangerouslySetInnerHTML The `CheckboxInput` component uses the `placeholderHTML` prop with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without sanitization. Since this prop originates from user configuration in `additionalSignUpFields`, it creates a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability, matching CVE-2019-20174.

### Bug: Open redirect vulnerability via protocol-relative URL bypass The redirect URL validation can be bypassed using a double-slash after the origin. When a user-controlled `redirect` parameter like `https://legitimate-site.com//evil.com` is provided, the origin check passes since both origins match. However, after stripping the origin with `redirect.substr(urlParams.origin.length)`, the result is `//evil.com` - a protocol-relative URL that redirects users to `evil.com`. This enables open redirect attacks for phishing.

### Bug: XSS vulnerability via unsanitized placeholder in dangerouslySetInnerHTML The `placeholder` prop is rendered directly using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without any sanitization. This is the exact vulnerability pattern for CVE-2019-20174, which allows Cross-Site Scripting attacks when the `placeholder` value contains malicious HTML or JavaScript. An attacker who can control the placeholder content (such as through `additionalSignUpFields` configuration) can inject and execute arbitrary scripts in the user's browser.

### Bug: Open redirect allows redirecting users to malicious sites The redirect handling contains an open redirect vulnerability (CVE-2019-18350). When the `redirect` URL parameter has a different origin than the current site, the code redirects directly to that external URL via `window.location.href = redirect`. This allows attackers to craft login URLs that redirect victims to malicious phishing sites after successful authentication. The origin check on line 50 should reject non-matching origins entirely rather than redirecting to them.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: NoSQL injection allows password reset token bypass The `code` parameter in `changePassword` is only validated with `!code`, which checks for truthiness but not type. An attacker can submit `code` as a JSON object (e.g., `{"$gt":""}`) which passes the truthiness check but causes the database query `findOne({ resetPasswordToken: code })` to match any administrator with a non-empty reset token. This is the exact vulnerability pattern of CVE-2019-18818, enabling complete authentication bypass for password resets.

### Bug: User-controlled URL enables password reset phishing attacks The `forgotPassword` function accepts a user-controlled `url` parameter from the request body and embeds it directly in the password reset email at line 332. An attacker can provide their own malicious URL, causing the password reset link to redirect users to an attacker-controlled site. This enables phishing attacks where attackers can capture the reset token or steal credentials.

### Bug: Missing argument causes inconsistent error response format The `ctx.badRequest` call for missing `passwordConfirmation` validation is missing the `null` first argument that all other error responses in this file use. Every other call follows the pattern `ctx.badRequest(null, formatError(...))`, but this one passes `formatError(...)` as the first argument directly. This causes the error response format to be inconsistent, with the formatted error object being interpreted as the message parameter instead of the data parameter.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Missing first argument causes inconsistent error formatting The `ctx.badRequest` call for missing `passwordConfirmation` is missing the `null` first argument. All other error calls in this file use `ctx.badRequest(null, formatError(...))`, but this one passes `formatError(...)` as the first argument directly. This causes the formatted error object to be interpreted as the message parameter rather than the body parameter, resulting in inconsistent error response format for this specific validation.

### Bug: User-controlled URL enables password reset poisoning attack The `url` parameter is taken directly from user input and embedded in the password reset email without any validation. An attacker can supply a malicious URL pointing to their own server. When the legitimate admin receives the email and clicks the link, the password reset token is sent to the attacker's server, allowing them to hijack the admin account. This is a password reset poisoning vulnerability.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/strapi-admin/controllers/Auth.js#L331-L332`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2019-18818-fixed-bugbot/blob/4f126c6d466f6f143d3fcf8bfd788ae0eca10299/packages/strapi-admin/controllers/Auth.js#L331-L332)

### Bug: Missing return statement in error catch block The `ctx.badRequest` call in the catch block of the `register` function is missing a `return` statement. All other `ctx.badRequest` calls in this file use `return ctx.badRequest(...)` to ensure the function terminates after sending the error response. While this is currently at the end of the function, the inconsistency could cause issues if code is added afterward, and it deviates from the established pattern used everywhere else in this controller.

### Bug: Insufficient type validation allows password reset bypass The `!code` check only validates that `code` is truthy, not that it's actually a string. If an attacker passes `code` as an array like `[""]`, it passes the falsy check (arrays are truthy), but `${[""]}` converts to an empty string `""`. This could potentially match admin records with empty or unset `resetPasswordToken` values. The code parameter needs explicit string type validation to prevent this bypass. This is the core vulnerability pattern related to CVE-2019-18818.

### Bug: Email parameter lacks type validation for database query The `email` parameter from user input is used directly in the database query at `findOne({ email })` without validating that it's a string. If an attacker sends a JSON object as `email` (such as a MongoDB query operator), it could be interpreted by the database layer, potentially leading to NoSQL injection or information disclosure about which emails exist in the system.

### Bug: Memory exposure via uninitialized Buffer allocation This code contains CVE-2017-16026. When `chunked` is false, the `add` function calls `new Buffer(part)`. If `part.body` is a number (line 86), `new Buffer(number)` allocates an uninitialized buffer of that size, exposing potentially sensitive process memory (passwords, keys, etc.). An attacker can set `part.body` to a number to leak arbitrary amounts of process memory in the response.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/multipart.js#L85-L86`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2017-16026-unfixed-bugbot/blob/3fe37d5d20b4784f7acf14c17376f021fb95af33/lib/multipart.js#L85-L86)

### Bug: Error emitted without stopping execution causes crash When `parts` lacks a `forEach` method, an error is emitted but execution continues without returning. This causes the code to crash on line 33 when `parts.forEach()` is called anyway. The error handler provides a false sense of graceful error handling while the code still attempts to use the invalid `parts` object.

This means undefined values will later be passed to `add(part.body)` in the `build` function, potentially causing `new Buffer(undefined)` to be called, which creates a zero-length buffer rather than failing gracefully.

### Bug: CRLF injection allows header/content manipulation in multipart The code concatenates part keys and values directly into the multipart preamble without sanitizing CRLF sequences. If a key or value contains `\r\n`, an attacker could inject additional headers or terminate the header section early with `\r\n\r\n` to inject arbitrary content into the multipart body. This allows manipulation of the multipart structure.

### Bug: Boundary extraction regex failure corrupts boundary value The `indexOf('boundary')` check passes if "boundary" appears anywhere in the header (even as a substring of another word), but the regex `/.*boundary=([^\s;]+).*/` requires `boundary=` followed by a non-empty value. When the regex doesn't match (e.g., empty value like `boundary=` or "boundary" as substring), `replace` returns the entire header string as the boundary, creating malformed multipart requests.

### Bug: Prototype pollution via unsanitized object key assignment The `mergeKeys` function assigns properties to objects without sanitizing dangerous keys like `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`. When an attacker passes input containing `__proto__` as an own property (e.g., via `JSON.parse`), the assignment `merged[key] = ...` pollutes `Object.prototype`, affecting all objects in the application. review_comments.body: ### Bug: Deprecated Buffer constructor enables memory disclosure vulnerability Using `new Buffer(part)` is the root cause of CVE-2017-16026. While the code checks for numbers at lines 71-73 and converts them to strings, this mitigation is incomplete. If `part.body` is somehow not converted properly or if other code paths bypass the check, passing a numeric value to `new Buffer()` allocates a buffer of that size filled with uninitialized memory, potentially exposing sensitive data. The deprecated `Buffer` constructor is inherently unsafe and `Buffer.from()` is the recommended replacement.

### Bug: Regex failure silently corrupts boundary with entire header The check at line 58 only verifies the word "boundary" exists in the header, but the regex on line 59 requires a non-empty value after `boundary=`. If the header contains "boundary" without a valid value (e.g., `multipart/form-data; boundary=`), the regex won't match and `replace()` returns the entire original header string. This corrupts `self.boundary` with the full header text, producing malformed multipart body output when used in the `build` method.

### Bug: ReDoS vulnerability in header parsing regex patterns The `EXT_LIST` regex used in `parseHeader` is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attacks (CVE-2020-7662). The nested quantifiers in the combined regex patterns—specifically ` *` inside `(?: ... )*` constructs—cause catastrophic backtracking when processing specially crafted header strings. An attacker can provide malicious input to `parseHeader` that causes the regex engine to hang, leading to denial of service.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/parser.js#L5-L8`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2020-7662-unfixed-bugbot/blob/297ef556190e4dd7af366c6467549aa79ce5cab1/lib/parser.js#L5-L8)

### Bug: Global flag on regex causes inconsistent test results The `NOTOKEN` regex is defined with the `g` (global) flag, but it's used with `.test()` in `serializeParams`. Regexes with the `g` flag maintain state via `lastIndex`, causing `.test()` to start searching from a non-zero position on subsequent calls. This means values containing non-token characters may incorrectly fail the test and not be properly quoted, depending on what previous values were processed.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/parser.js#L62-L63`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2020-7662-unfixed-bugbot/blob/297ef556190e4dd7af366c6467549aa79ce5cab1/lib/parser.js#L62-L63)

When `parseHeader` receives a malicious header containing an unclosed string with repeating backslash sequences, the regex engine exhibits quadratic backtracking behavior, allowing attackers to cause CPU exhaustion and denial of service.

### Bug: Global regex flag causes incorrect test results across calls The `NOTOKEN` regex is defined with the global `g` flag, which causes `lastIndex` state to persist between `.test()` calls. When `serializeParams` processes multiple string values, a successful match sets `lastIndex` to a non-zero value, causing subsequent `.test()` calls to start mid-string and potentially return incorrect results. This can result in values that contain non-token characters being serialized without proper quoting.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/parser.js#L62-L63`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2020-7662-fixed-bugbot/blob/b2dd5c19247ea5cce2c6ffaf059d1134b27ea480/lib/parser.js#L62-L63)

### Bug: Prototype pollution vulnerability in deep merge function The `mergeKeys` function lacks proper sanitization of dangerous keys like `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype`. While the check `merged[key] !== Object.getPrototypeOf(merged)` on line 80 attempts to prevent recursing into the prototype chain, it's an incomplete protection. When an attacker controls the input structure (e.g., via `JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {"polluted": true}}')`), the `__proto__` key becomes an own enumerable property that `getEnumerableOwnPropertyKeys` will include. This allows prototype pollution attacks where malicious properties can be injected into `Object.prototype`, affecting all objects in the application. This is the CVE-2018-3752 vulnerability.

### Bug: Incorrect globalThis assignment shadows built-in global reference The assignment `const globalThis = this` captures the wrong value. In Node.js modules with `'use strict'`, `this` at the top level is `module.exports` (an empty object `{}`), not the actual global object. This variable also shadows the built-in `globalThis` available in modern JavaScript. As a result, the check `this !== globalThis` on line 145 compares against `{}` instead of the real global object, causing the merge options detection logic to behave incorrectly.
Additional Locations (1) - [`index.js#L144-L145`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3752-fixed-bugbot/blob/b6d5bc321b3c6f2eac227cc3cc20d0f2450a90e2/index.js#L144-L145)

### Bug: OS command injection via unsanitized shell command execution The `exec` call on Windows that uses `OPENCV_DIR` directly introduces an OS command injection vulnerability (CVE-2019-10061). If an attacker controls the `OPENCV_DIR` environment variable, they can execute arbitrary commands due to the lack of input sanitization.

### Bug: Windows fallback always throws error for "--exists" flag The `flag` variable is hardcoded to `"--exists"`, but the `printPaths` function, called during the Windows fallback, only handles `"--cflags"` and `"--libs"`. This mismatch causes `printPaths` to throw an error for an unknown argument, rendering the Windows fallback non-functional.
Additional Locations (1) - [`utils/find-opencv.js#L4-L5`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2019-10061-fixed-bugbot/blob/d6614a7fbe7fe3fa210483ba61718ffb7f000752/utils/find-opencv.js#L4-L5)

### Bug: Command injection via unsanitized command line argument The `flag` variable is taken directly from `process.argv[2]` without validation and concatenated into a shell command passed to `exec()`. An attacker can inject arbitrary commands by providing malicious input like `"; rm -rf /"` as a command line argument. This is the known vulnerability CVE-2019-10061. User input passed to shell execution functions needs to be sanitized or `execFile` with an argument array should be used instead.
Additional Locations (1) - [`utils/find-opencv.js#L4-L5`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2019-10061-unfixed-bugbot/blob/bfc64e520e5e2b97715ebdfa8e1ff0339d411a4e/utils/find-opencv.js#L4-L5)

### Bug: Error constructor ignores additional arguments silently The `Error` constructor only accepts a single string argument for the message. The additional arguments `opencv` and `flag` are silently ignored and won't appear in the error message. The developer likely intended to concatenate these values into the message string to provide useful debugging information.

### Bug: Environment variable check never matches after string truncation The `cleanupEchoOutput` function on line 34 removes the last 2 characters from stdout (presumably `\r\n`). When `OPENCV_DIR` is undefined on Windows, echo outputs `%OPENCV_DIR%\r\n`, which after cleanup becomes `%OPENCV_DIR` (missing the trailing `%`). The comparison on line 38 against the full string `"%OPENCV_DIR%"` will never match, so the intended "OPENCV_DIR doesn't seem to be defined" error will never be thrown.
Additional Locations (1) - [`utils/find-opencv.js#L33-L34`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2019-10061-unfixed-bugbot/blob/bfc64e520e5e2b97715ebdfa8e1ff0339d411a4e/utils/find-opencv.js#L33-L34)

### Bug: Prototype pollution in deepCopy allows object injection The `deepCopy` function iterates over all properties in the source object using `for (var name in source)` without checking if `name` is `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`. This allows an attacker to pollute the Object prototype by passing a crafted payload like `JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {"polluted": true}}')`, which would inject properties into all JavaScript objects. The `deepCreate` function has the same vulnerability pattern.
Additional Locations (1) - [`request/util.js#L81-L95`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2020-5258-unfixed-bugbot/blob/84e37931e694bb7652b45222d8a66ddf973069bb/request/util.js#L81-L95)

### Bug: deepCopyArray crashes when array contains null values The `deepCopyArray` function uses `typeof svalItem === 'object'` to check if array items need deep copying, but `typeof null === 'object'` in JavaScript. When an array contains `null` values, this causes `deepCopy({}, null)` to be called, which then throws a TypeError when `for (var name in source)` attempts to iterate over `null`. The main `deepCopy` function avoids this by using `shouldDeepCopy()` which checks `value &&` first.

### Bug: Prototype pollution via constructor.prototype in deepCopy The `deepCopy` function is vulnerable to prototype pollution via the `constructor.prototype` path, as it only blocks `__proto__`. Additionally, `deepCopyArray` incorrectly handles `null` elements, leading to a `TypeError`, and converts nested arrays into plain objects instead of deep copying them as arrays.

### Bug: Sandbox escape allows arbitrary code execution The sandbox escape protection at line 42 (`this.constructor.constructor = function () {}`) is ineffective. When the constructed function is called with `.call(null, __context)`, `this` is `null` or the global object, not the intended context. More critically, attackers can still access the `Function` constructor through alternative prototype chains like `[].constructor.constructor` or `"".constructor.constructor` to escape the sandbox and execute arbitrary code. This is the known CVE-2019-10759 vulnerability.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Missing return after resolve causes double promise settlement When `statusCode` equals `HttpCodes.NotFound` (404), the promise is resolved but execution continues without returning. Since 404 > 299, the code proceeds to call `reject(err)` later. While only the first settlement takes effect, this represents a logic error where both `resolve` and `reject` are called for 404 responses.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Global HTTPS agent options mutated affecting entire process When `_keepAlive` is false and no proxy is used, `_getAgent` assigns `https.globalAgent` to `agent` at line 661. If `_ignoreSslError` is true, lines 668-670 mutate `agent.options` by setting `rejectUnauthorized: false`. This modifies the global agent's options, disabling SSL certificate verification for ALL HTTPS requests in the entire Node.js process, not just this client's requests.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Stream errors unhandled causing potential request hang When `data` is a stream, the code listens for `close` event and pipes to the request, but doesn't register an error handler on the stream. If the input stream emits an `error` event, the error is unhandled and the request may hang indefinitely since `req.end()` is never called and `handleResult` is never invoked with the error.

+        let authenticationHandler: ifm.IRequestHandler
+
+        for (let i = 0; i < this.handlers.length; i++) {
+          if (this.handlers[i].canHandleAuthentication(response)) {
+            authenticationHandler = this.handlers[i]
+            break
+          }
+        }
+
+        if (authenticationHandler) {
+          return authenticationHandler.handleAuthentication(this, info, data)
+        } else {
+          // We have received an unauthorized response but have no handlers to handle it.
+          // Let the response return to the caller.
+          return response
+        }
+      }
+
+      let redirectsRemaining: number = this._maxRedirects
+      while (
+        HttpRedirectCodes.indexOf(response.message.statusCode) != -1 &&
+        this._allowRedirects &&
+        redirectsRemaining > 0
+      ) {
+        const redirectUrl: string | null = response.message.headers['location']
+        if (!redirectUrl) {
+          // if there's no location to redirect to, we won't
+          break
+        }
+        let parsedRedirectUrl = url.parse(redirectUrl)
+        if (
+          parsedUrl.protocol == 'https:' &&
+          parsedUrl.protocol != parsedRedirectUrl.protocol &&
+          !this._allowRedirectDowngrade
+        ) {
+          throw new Error(
+            'Redirect from HTTPS to HTTP protocol. This downgrade is not allowed for security reasons. If you want to allow this behavior, set the allowRedirectDowngrade option to true.'
+          )
+        }

+        // we need to finish reading the response before reassigning response
+        // which will leak the open socket.
+        await response.readBody()
+
+        // strip authorization header if redirected to a different hostname
+        if (parsedRedirectUrl.hostname !== parsedUrl.hostname) {
+          for (let header in headers) {
+            // header names are case insensitive
+            if (header.toLowerCase() === 'authorization') {
+              delete headers[header]
+            }
+          }
+        }
+
+        // let's make the request with the new redirectUrl
+        info = this._prepareRequest(verb, parsedRedirectUrl, headers)
+        response = await this.requestRaw(info, data)
+        redirectsRemaining--
+      }
+
+      if (HttpResponseRetryCodes.indexOf(response.message.statusCode) == -1) {
+        // If not a retry code, return immediately instead of retrying
+        return response
+      }
+
+      numTries += 1
+
+      if (numTries < maxTries) {
+        await response.readBody()
+        await this._performExponentialBackoff(numTries)
+      }
+    }

+    return response
+  }

+    if (this._agent) {
+      this._agent.destroy()

+    this._disposed = true
+  }

+  /**
+   * Raw request.
+   * @param info
+   * @param data
+   */
