+    info: ifm.IRequestInfo,
+    data: string | NodeJS.ReadableStream
+  ): Promise<ifm.IHttpClientResponse> {
+    return new Promise<ifm.IHttpClientResponse>((resolve, reject) => {
+      let callbackForResult = function (
+        err: any,
+        res: ifm.IHttpClientResponse
+      ) {
+        if (err) {
+          reject(err)
+        }
+
+        resolve(res)
+      }
+
+      this.requestRawWithCallback(info, data, callbackForResult)
+    })
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Raw request with callback.
+   * @param info
+   * @param data
+   * @param onResult
+   */
+  public requestRawWithCallback(
+    info: ifm.IRequestInfo,
+    data: string | NodeJS.ReadableStream,
+    onResult: (err: any, res: ifm.IHttpClientResponse) => void
+  ): void {
+    let socket
+
+    if (typeof data === 'string') {
+      info.options.headers['Content-Length'] = Buffer.byteLength(data, 'utf8')
+    }
+
+    let callbackCalled: boolean = false
+    let handleResult = (err: any, res: HttpClientResponse) => {
+      if (!callbackCalled) {
+        callbackCalled = true
+        onResult(err, res)
+      }
+    }
+
+    let req: http.ClientRequest = info.httpModule.request(
+      info.options,
+      (msg: http.IncomingMessage) => {
+        let res: HttpClientResponse = new HttpClientResponse(msg)
+        handleResult(null, res)
+      }
+    )
+
+    req.on('socket', sock => {
+      socket = sock
+    })
+
+    // If we ever get disconnected, we want the socket to timeout eventually
+    req.setTimeout(this._socketTimeout || 3 * 60000, () => {
+      if (socket) {
+        socket.end()
+      }
+      handleResult(new Error('Request timeout: ' + info.options.path), null)
+    })
+
+    req.on('error', function (err) {
+      // err has statusCode property
+      // res should have headers
+      handleResult(err, null)
+    })
+
+    if (data && typeof data === 'string') {
+      req.write(data, 'utf8')
+    }
+
+    if (data && typeof data !== 'string') {
+      data.on('close', function () {
+        req.end()
+      })
+
+      data.pipe(req)

review_comments.body:
### Bug: Path traversal vulnerability allows reading arbitrary files The path traversal protection is insufficient (CVE-2018-3713). The `resolveUrl` function only checks for literal `..` sequences using `includes("..")`, but this can be bypassed. Additionally, the regex `replace(/^(\.\.[\/\\])+/, '')` on line 72 only removes `..` patterns from the BEGINNING of the path, not embedded traversal sequences. An attacker can exploit this to read arbitrary files outside the intended serving directory by crafting requests that bypass these incomplete checks.
Additional Locations (1) - [`angular-http-server.js#L71-L74`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3713-unfixed-bugbot/blob/9d38d281f4a2c0adf9bb2ddef439bbea478802e7/angular-http-server.js#L71-L74)

### Bug: HTTPS flag ignored when opening browser URL The URL protocol selection only checks `argv.ssl` but not `argv.https`. The server startup on line 23 accepts either `--ssl` or `--https` to enable HTTPS mode, but the browser URL construction only checks `argv.ssl`. When a user starts the server with `--https --open`, the server runs in HTTPS mode but the browser incorrectly opens an HTTP URL, causing a connection failure.

### Bug: Sandbox escape allows arbitrary code execution The sandbox implementation is vulnerable to escape attacks (CVE-2019-10759). The attempt to disable the `Function` constructor by setting `this.constructor.constructor = function () {}` is ineffective because attackers can access the `Function` constructor through any function's prototype chain, e.g., `(function(){}).constructor("return this")()`. This allows untrusted code to break out of the sandbox and execute arbitrary code with full privileges.

review_comments.body: ### Bug: Undefined Exception class causes runtime error The code uses `throw new Exception(...)` but `Exception` is not defined in JavaScript/Node.js. The correct constructor is `Error`. When an invalid port number is provided, this will throw a `ReferenceError: Exception is not defined` instead of the intended error message, causing confusing error output and potentially different error handling behavior.

### Bug: Intentionally vulnerable CVE test code added to repository The PR title explicitly states this file is a "vulnerable file for bugbot analysis - CVE-2018-3713" which is a known path traversal vulnerability in angular-http-server. Adding intentionally vulnerable code to a repository, even for testing purposes, poses security risks if accidentally deployed or if the test boundaries are unclear. This appears to be test/analysis code that likely shouldn't be committed to production branches.

### Bug: Missing error handling in certificate creation callback The `pem.createCertificate` callback receives an `err` parameter but never checks it. If certificate creation fails, `keys` will be undefined, and accessing `keys.serviceKey` and `keys.certificate` will throw a runtime error. The error should be checked before using the `keys` object.

### Bug: HTTPS flag check inconsistent when opening browser The server starts with HTTPS when either `argv.ssl` or `argv.https` is set (line 25), but the browser URL scheme check on line 43 only considers `argv.ssl`. When a user starts the server with `--https`, the browser will incorrectly open an `http://` URL instead of `https://`, causing a connection failure.
Additional Locations (1) - [`angular-http-server.js#L24-L25`](https://github.com/unnxt30/CVE-2018-3713-fixed-bugbot/blob/9d7229bcc303ad6f728c7585bb540d343ea86202/angular-http-server.js#L24-L25)

Since `getURLMeta` defaults `blockLocalIPs` to `false`, this allows the metadata fetch to access local/internal IPs in production, creating an SSRF vulnerability. An attacker could probe internal network resources through this endpoint. The `!debug` parameter needs to be passed consistently, as done on line 30 and line 69.

The `handleChunk` method in `Uploader` is designed to receive errors as the first parameter and properly handle cleanup and client notification. Since errors are silently swallowed, when a download fails the uploader will never know, leaving uploads in a hanging/incomplete state and never notifying the client of the failure.
